laws.k: domestic-workers|BO|Law No. 2450 regulating salaried household work
laws.t: Law No. 2450 regulating salaried household work
laws.tp: Minimum wage, hours, rest and leave for household workers.
laws.s2: Upah minimum, jam kerja, istirahat, dan cuti bagi pekerja rumah tangga.

coded.vl: General labor law applies, or a dedicated statute grants its core rights
coded.n: Dedicated statute on salaried household work.

coded.fn: Written contract in a language understood
coded.vl: Written contract required, no language rule
Statutory minimum wage applies on the same terms as other workers
Periodic payment required, without further safeguards
Only a daily rest rule, or a longer limit than for other workers
coded.n: 8 hours for live-out, 10 for live-in workers.

coded.vl: At least 24 consecutive hours, not replaceable by pay at the employer's request
Equal to or longer than for other workers

coded.fn: Keeping own identity and travel documents
coded.vl: General rule only, not specific to domestic workers or without a penalty
Accommodation standards only; living in may be required
coded.n: Accommodation and food for live-in workers.

coded.vl: Worker may change employer without the employer's consent
coded.n: Residence not tied to one employer.

coded.vl: Courts or labor tribunals on the same terms as other workers, or fee-free
Partial: medical care, injury cover or employer insurance only

coded.fn: Protection from abuse, harassment and violence
coded.vl: General criminal or civil law only
May form and join trade unions

dec.pe: A Peruvian family asked for asylum in Bolivia and were sent back to Peru within days. The Inter-American Court said Bolivia should have heard their claim properly.
dec.pi: Sebuah keluarga Peru meminta suaka di Bolivia dan dipulangkan ke Peru dalam hitungan hari. Mahkamah Inter-Amerika menyatakan Bolivia seharusnya memeriksa permohonan mereka dengan benar.
